The Agent SDK spawns and supervises a `claude` CLI subprocess that owns a shell, a working directory, and session files on disk.
This page covers self-hosting on your own infrastructure.
None of them survive a container restart, a scale-down, or a move to a different node.

Three things to know about how `SessionStore` behaves:

* **Transcripts only**: `SessionStore` mirrors transcripts, not `CLAUDE.md` memory files or other working-directory artifacts. Mount a shared volume or sync those separately.
* **Mirror, not replacement**: the subprocess writes to local disk first, and the SDK forwards a copy of each batch to the store. A fresh session's local transcript outlives the run; a run resumed from the store deletes its local copy at the end, so the store holds the only durable copy. See [Dual-write architecture](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage.md#dual-write-architecture).
* **`mirror_error` messages**: when the SDK can't deliver a batch to the store, it drops the batch, emits a `{ type: "system", subtype: "mirror_error" }` message, and continues the query. Alert on these if store durability matters. See [Mirror writes are best-effort](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/session-storage.md#mirror-writes-are-best-effort) for the retry and timeout behavior.

### Observability

Agent SDK agents are long-lived processes that spawn tool calls across many API round-trips. Without telemetry you cannot see which tools ran, how long they took, or where a session stalled.

The SDK inherits OpenTelemetry configuration from the environment. Set the OTEL environment variables at the container or orchestrator level so every `query()` call exports spans, metrics, and log events to your collector.

The SDK inherits OpenTelemetry configuration from the environment. Set the OTEL environment variables at the container or orchestrator level so every `query()` call exports spans, metrics, and log events to your collector.

```bash title=".env" theme={null}
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1
CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://collector.example.com:4318
```

Prompt text and tool inputs are not included in exports by default.

The SDK needs outbound HTTPS to `api.anthropic.com`, or to your provider's regional endpoint when running on Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform.
Requires TypeScript Agent SDK v0.3.234 or later, or Python Agent SDK v0.2.140 or later.

## Limitations The custom MCP server has the following limitations: - **Server-Sent Events (SSE)**: The older `SSE` transport isn't supported. The connector exclusively supports the newer `StreamableHTTP` transport. - **TLS certificate requirement**: Configure custom MCP servers with a TLS certificate signed by a publicly trusted Certificate Authority (CA), with the following exception: * **Private MCP servers with Agent Gateway**: If you route egress traffic through Agent Gateway, you can use private CAs or self-signed certificates by configuring custom TLS trust anchors (`tlsConfig`) in your [agent connectivity template](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/set-up-vpc-connectivity#tls-certificate-requirements). - **Actions limit**: To ensure optimal performance, limit the number of enabled actions in your custom MCP server data store to 100 at a time. For more information, see [Enable actions](#enable-actions). - **Agent Gateway binding limit**: A Gemini Enterprise app binds to a single egress Agent Gateway, but multiple Gemini Enterprise apps can share the same Agent Gateway. - **App-scoped creation**: You can't link a standalone Custom MCP server data store to a Gemini Enterprise app. Create the data store directly within your app under **Connected Data Stores**. - **VPC Service Controls**: Egress controls are enforced through organization policy constraints, such as `allowedEgressFqdns` and `allowedDataSources`, rather than runtime traffic enforcement. Custom MCP servers are supported in VPC Service Controls-enabled projects when you explicitly allow the required egress domains and data sources. For more information, see [Override the organization policy for Custom MCP data stores](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/custom-mcp-server/override-constraint-for-custom-mcp-data-stores). ## Before you begin Before you set up your custom MCP server connection, ensure you perform the following: - Several organization policy constraints apply to Custom MCP data stores. You must: * Override the organization policy constraint that blocks Custom MCP data store creation. For more information, see [Override the organization policy for Custom MCP data stores](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/custom-mcp-server/override-constraint-for-custom-mcp-data-stores). * Explicitly allow the fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) for your custom MCP server URL, authorization URL, and token URL. For more information, see [Configure allowed egress FQDNs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/configure-allowed-egress-fqdns). **Note:** You only need to add the domain name, not the full URL. For example, for an MCP server URL of `https://api.cymbal.com/mcp` with authorization and token URLs on `auth.cymbal.com`, allow both `api.cymbal.com` and `auth.cymbal.com`. * If project enforcement is enabled or the project is VPC Service Controls-protected, you must add `custom_mcp` to the allowed data sources. See [Configure allowed data sources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/configure-allowed-data-sources). * If you route egress traffic through Agent Gateway, ensure your project organization policy permits binding your Gemini Enterprise app to the gateway. For more information, see [Restrict Gemini Enterprise binding to approved Agent Gateways](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-ge-deploy#restrict-ge). - Optional: If your custom MCP server is hosted inside a private Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network, complete the prerequisite network attachment, gateway, and firewall configurations. For details, see [Prerequisites to set up a custom MCP server data store with VPC connectivity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/custom-mcp-server/set-up-vpc-custom-mcp-server). - Grant the **Discovery Engine Editor** role (`roles/discoveryengine.editor`). This role is required for your administrator to create the data store. To grant this role, do the following: 1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the **IAM** page. [Go to IAM](https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/iam) 2. Locate the user account, and click the edit **Edit** icon. 3. Grant the **Discovery Engine Editor** role to your user. For more information, see [IAM roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control). - Register Gemini Enterprise as an OAuth client application with your identity provider (for example, Okta, Azure AD, or Google). To register the app, do the following: 1. Set the authorization redirect URL to `https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect`. 2. Grant necessary OAuth scopes to the client app. After you register the client app, obtain the `client_id` and `client_secret` that are needed for configuring the custom MCP server data store in the following steps. - If your custom MCP server is hosted on Cloud Run and requires authentication, grant the **Cloud Run Invoker** (`roles/run.invoker`) role to the service agent. For more information, see [Set up authentication for a custom MCP server on Cloud Run](#cloud_run_authentication). ## Set up authentication for a custom MCP server on Cloud Run If your custom MCP server is hosted on Cloud Run and requires authentication, Gemini Enterprise can securely connect to private services that don't allow public access. ### How authentication works When you connect to a Cloud Run service, Gemini Enterprise automatically sends the following authorization headers in each request: - **`X-Serverless-Authorization`** : Contains a Google-signed ID token that authenticates the Gemini Enterprise service agent. - **`Authorization`** : Preserves the user's OAuth token intact. **Note**: Gemini Enterprise automatically sends the Google-signed ID token only when you connect to a default Cloud Run URL that ends in `.run.app`. Gemini Enterprise doesn't send the ID token if your service uses a custom domain. ### Grant access to the service agent To authorize Gemini Enterprise to invoke your private Cloud Run service, grant the **Cloud Run Invoker** (`roles/run.invoker`) role to the Gemini Enterprise service agent on the receiving service. The service agent email uses the following format: `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-discoveryengine.iam.gserviceaccount.com` Replace `PROJECT_NUMBER` with the project number of the Google Cloud project that hosts your Gemini Enterprise app. For instructions on how to grant IAM roles on a service, see [Authenticating service-to-service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service). ## Create the custom MCP server data store **Note:** By default, outbound traffic to your custom MCP server doesn't route through [Agent Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-ge-deploy) unless you select **Route egress through Agent Gateway** on the **MCP Server Configuration** page. To set up the configuration flow, follow these steps: 1. In the Google Cloud console, go to the **Gemini Enterprise** page. [Gemini Enterprise](https://console.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/) 2. In the navigation menu, click **Apps**, and then select the app that requires custom MCP data store connectivity. 3. Click **Connected Data Stores**. 4. Click add **New data store**. 5. On the **Select a data source** page, enter *Custom MCP Server* into the **Search sources** field. The **Custom MCP Server** card displays. 6. Click **Add MCP server**. The **MCP Server Configuration** page displays. 7. Optional: To route outbound traffic through Agent Gateway, select the **Route egress through Agent Gateway** checkbox. Select this option for either of the following scenarios: - **Private network hosting**: You host your custom MCP server privately inside a VPC network. - **Static IP egress**: You host your custom MCP server externally (such as on-premises or with a third-party provider) and require incoming requests to originate from reserved static IP addresses. Routing traffic through Agent Gateway into your VPC network lets you egress traffic through a gateway with fixed IP addresses, so you can configure IP-based firewall allowlists on your external server. **Note:** This setting only routes tool calls sent to your custom MCP server through Agent Gateway. Other traffic, such as AI model processing and document search, doesn't pass through the gateway. If you leave this checkbox unselected, Gemini Enterprise connects to your MCP server directly over the public internet. In the **Engine resource name** field, enter the resource name of the engine that egress traffic routes to in the following format: ``` projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/collections/default_collection/engines/APP_ID ``` Replace the following: - `PROJECT_NUMBER`: Your Google Cloud project number. - `LOCATION`: The location of your app, such as `global`, `us`, or `eu`. - `APP_ID`: The ID of your app. ### How to obtain your engine resource name If you don't know your app's engine resource name, you can list the engines in your project using the Discovery Engine API: ``` curl -s -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "X-Goog-User-Project: PROJECT_ID" \ "https://ENDPOINT_LOCATION-discoveryengine.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/collections/default_collection/engines" \ | jq -r '.engines[]? | "App Name: \(.displayName)\nEngine Resource Name: \(.name)\n"' ``` Replace the following: - `PROJECT_ID`: the ID of your project. - `ENDPOINT_LOCATION`: the multi-region for your API request. Specify one of the following values: * `us` for the US multi-region * `eu` for the EU multi-region * `global` for the Global location For more information, see [Specify a multi-region for your data store](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations#specify_a_multi-region_for_your_data_store). - `PROJECT_NUMBER`: the number of your Google Cloud project. - `LOCATION`: the location of your app (such as `global`, `us`, or `eu`). Example output: ``` App Name: Cymbal Math App Engine Resource Name: projects/1234567890/locations/global/collections/default_collection/engines/chat-app-cymbal ``` For more information, see [`projects.locations.collections.engines.list`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.collections.engines/list). 8. In the **Authentication settings** section, select one of the following options: - **OAuth 2.0**: Select this option to add authentication. 1. Enter the values in the following required fields: | Field | Description | | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **MCP Server URL** | This is the endpoint where your MCP server is hosted. It must be an HTTPS URL. Gemini Enterprise only supports the `StreamableHTTP` transport. The URL often ends with `/mcp`. For example, `https://mcp.cymbal.com/mcp`.
**Note**: If your server is hosted on Cloud Run, enter your default service URL ending in `.run.app`. Gemini Enterprise automatically sends a Google-signed ID token for IAM authentication. | | **Authorization URL** | The base URL for the user to authorize Gemini Enterprise to access your MCP server. For example, `https://mcp.cymbal.com/authorize`.
**Note**: Enter only the base URL, without query parameters. Gemini Enterprise automatically appends standard OAuth parameters (such as `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, and `scope`) during authorization. If your authorization server requires additional parameters, specify them in the **Authorization URL Parameters** field. | | **Authorization URL Parameters** | Optional. Any additional parameters required by your authorization URL. For example, to get a refresh token from a Google MCP server, enter `&access_type=offline&prompt=consent`.
If your authorization server requires an `audience` parameter, you can add it as a parameter in this setting. For example, `&audience=https://api.cymbal.com/v1/`. | | **Token URL** | The endpoint used to exchange the authorization code for an access token during OAuth authentication. For example, `https://mcp.cymbal.com/token`. | | **Client ID** | The unique identifier of the OAuth app that you registered in your identity provider to represent Gemini Enterprise. | | **Client Secret** | The confidential key associated with the OAuth app that you registered in your identity provider to represent Gemini Enterprise. | | **Scopes** | The permissions that define what actions Gemini Enterprise can perform on behalf of a user, or what data it can access on the MCP server. Gemini Enterprise requests these scopes during user authorization. Configure your OAuth app to support these scopes.
When you specify scopes, consider the following:
Provide a space-separated list of scopes. For example, for Box, you provide: `root_readwrite manage_managed_users manage_groups`.
Ensure the scopes provided are sufficient to let the user sign in and use the tools or actions enabled by the administrator; otherwise, the agent can't access your app.
A common scope is `offline_access`, which lets the app request a refresh token. | | **Enable PKCE Support** | Optional. Select this checkbox to enable Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE, RFC 7636) for additional OAuth security. Enable this setting if your MCP server's OAuth provider supports PKCE. | | **Use HTTP Basic Authentication** | Optional. Selected by default. Sends the client ID and client secret in the HTTP `Authorization` header using Basic authentication instead of in the token request body. | 2. Click **Verify Auth**. 3. Click **Continue**. - **No authentication**: Select this option if your MCP server doesn't require authentication. 1. Enter the **MCP Server URL**. This is the endpoint where your MCP server is hosted.

To enable Agent Gateway egress to your private network, the custom MCP server must be registered within your Gemini Enterprise app and configured to route private traffic through Agent Gateway (supported in `us-central1` and `europe-west1`).
Optional: In the **Sensitive data protection policy** field, enter the resource path of a Sensitive Data Protection policy to inspect and mask sensitive data in requests.

cited_texts: The Copilot harness is an optional [managed runtime](#understand-what-the-harness-changes) for prompt agents.

## Configure tools and skills

The Copilot harness supports:

- **Harness tools** for reading files, writing files, running shell commands, fetching web content, and delegating to subagents. New agents have all five tools enabled unless you [configure the harness tools](#configure-harness-tools).
- **Skills** referenced at the top level of the prompt agent definition.
- **Function tools** that your application executes and returns outputs for. See [Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/function-calling).
- **Foundry web search** added directly to the prompt agent definition without a project connection. The **Web** harness tool is separate and fetches content from a URL.
- **Compatible declared tools** that Foundry supplies through a managed toolbox. For the current list and each tool's configuration guidance, see [Create and manage a toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/toolbox#feature-support).

Tool availability can also depend on the project's region and model. A tool's existing authentication, connection, approval, and regional requirements still apply.

In `azure.yaml`, the prompt agent uses separate fields to attach capabilities and order their deployment:

| Agent field | What it does                                                                                                 |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `tools`     | Configures harness tools and directly attached declared tools.                                               |
| `skills`    | Attaches skills to the prompt agent.                                                                         |
| `toolboxes` | Attaches shared toolboxes to the prompt agent.                                                               |
| `uses`      | Orders sibling services for deployment. Adding a service to `uses` doesn't attach it to the agent by itself. |

Declare skills, connections, and toolboxes as sibling entries under `services`. Then reference their service keys from the agent's `skills`, `toolboxes`, and `uses` lists as shown in the following sections.

### Configure harness tools

The managed runtime includes built-in harness tools. These tools aren't tools that the agent calls through a project connection. The service and your organization's policy can restrict their availability.

During public preview, the service manages the approval policy for harness tools. The `require_approval` setting applies to customer-configured MCP tools, not harness tools.

| Harness tool          | What it enables                                   |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **File system read**  | Read and search files in the harness workspace.   |
| **File system write** | Create and modify files in the harness workspace. |

### Add a skill

Skills are versioned Foundry resources.
The `archive` field accepts a ZIP file or a directory with `SKILL.md` at its root.
[Bring your own model (BYOM)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/ai-gateway) isn't currently supported with the Copilot harness.

A sandbox isn't a customer-managed resource or durable output store. Store important outputs in Foundry Files or another durable service. A new conversation starts with separate history and a separate workspace.

## Create an agent

Create a new prompt agent and select the Copilot harness as its runtime. The harness selection is fixed for the agent during the initial public preview.

Before you create the agent, confirm that the project has a deployed model. If it doesn't, [deploy a model](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/tutorials/quickstart-create-foundry-resources#deploy-a-model).

1. Open [Microsoft Foundry](https://ai.azure.com/nextgen), ensure the **New Foundry** toggle is on, and select a project in a supported region. These steps apply to the new Microsoft Foundry experience, not Foundry (classic).
2. On the project home page, under **Build an agent**, select **Create an agent**.
3. Enter a unique agent name.
4. Keep interaction mode set to **Text**.
5. Select **Use the Microsoft Copilot harness**.
6. Select **Create** to open the playground.

After you change the model, instructions, tools, or skills, select **Save and start new chat**, and then wait for the new active version before testing it.

Set values for a unique agent name and a supported model:

```bash
AGENT_NAME="my-harness-agent-<unique-suffix>"
MODEL="<supported-model-name>"
```

To create a Foundry project, initialize the prompt agent interactively:

```bash
azd ai agent init "$AGENT_NAME" \
  --kind prompt \
  --agent-name "$AGENT_NAME" \
  --model "$MODEL"
```

When prompted, select **Create a new Foundry project**, and then choose a supported region and model deployment options.

To reuse an existing Foundry project and model deployment instead, set the project's full Azure resource ID and the deployment name. Initialize noninteractively:

```bash
PROJECT_ID="/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/<account>/projects/<project>"
MODEL_DEPLOYMENT="<model-deployment-name>"

azd ai agent init "$AGENT_NAME" \
  --no-prompt \
  --kind prompt \
  --agent-name "$AGENT_NAME" \
  --project-id "$PROJECT_ID" \
  --model-deployment "$MODEL_DEPLOYMENT"
```

After either initialization path finishes, open the generated directory:

```bash
cd "$AGENT_NAME"
```

In the generated `azure.yaml`, add the harness selection to the `azure.ai.agent` service. Keep the generated project, model, name, and other fields:

```yaml
services:
  <agent-service-name>:
    host: azure.ai.agent
    # Keep the generated agent fields.
    harness:
      type: microsoft_copilot_preview
```

Deploy the agent, and then inspect its persisted definition:

```bash
azd up --no-prompt
azd ai agent show --output json
```

Confirm that the agent is active and its definition contains `kind: prompt` and `harness.type: microsoft_copilot_preview` before you add tools or skills.

For an end-to-end scenario that adds web search and a reusable skill, see [Quickstart: Create a web research agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/quickstarts/create-web-research-agent?pivots=azd).

Use a new agent name and a model that supports reasoning and tool calling and is available to prompt agents in your project region. During the initial public preview, you can't add the Copilot harness to an existing prompt agent that uses the default runtime.

- [Python](#tabpanel_2_python)
- [C#](#tabpanel_2_csharp)
- [TypeScript](#tabpanel_2_typescript)
- [Java](#tabpanel_2_java)

```python
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.ai.projects.models import MicrosoftCopilotHarness, PromptAgentDefinition
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT = "your_project_endpoint"
FOUNDRY_AGENT_NAME = "your-agent-name"
FOUNDRY_MODEL = "your-model-name"

project = AIProjectClient(
  endpoint=FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT,
  credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
  allow_preview=True,
)
agent = project.agents.create_version(
  agent_name=FOUNDRY_AGENT_NAME,
  definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
    model=FOUNDRY_MODEL,
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant.",
    harness=MicrosoftCopilotHarness(),
  ),
)
print(f"Agent created: {agent.name}, version: {agent.version}")
```

The SDK selects the harness on the agent definition.

## Invoke and verify the agent

Start a new conversation, invoke the agent, and confirm that it returns a completed response. Each response request to an agent that uses the Copilot harness requires a conversation.

Important

Invoke a Copilot harness agent through its agent endpoint, not the project-level Responses endpoint, even when the request includes an agent reference. For URL examples and help with the HTTP 400 endpoint error, see [endpoint examples and troubleshooting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/faq#which-endpoint-should-i-use-to-invoke-a-copilot-harness-agent-).

1. In the playground, enter **What can you help me do?**, and then submit the message.
2. Confirm that the agent returns a completed response.
3. Open the response trace and confirm that it records the model activity for the request.

Start a new conversation and invoke the deployed agent:

```bash
azd ai agent invoke --new-conversation --no-prompt \
  "What can you help me do?"
```

Confirm that the command returns a completed text response.

Use an agent-scoped Responses client and an explicit conversation. Keep the project endpoint in the client initialization in the following examples; the agent name selects the agent-specific invocation route.

- [Python](#tabpanel_3_python)
- [C#](#tabpanel_3_csharp)
- [TypeScript](#tabpanel_3_typescript)
- [Java](#tabpanel_3_java)

```python
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT = "your_project_endpoint"
FOUNDRY_AGENT_NAME = "your-agent-name"

project = AIProjectClient(
  endpoint=FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT,
  credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
  allow_preview=True,
)
openai = project.get_openai_client(agent_name=FOUNDRY_AGENT_NAME)
conversation = openai.conversations.create()
response = openai.responses.create(
  conversation=conversation.id,
  input="What can you help me do?",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

Omit `store` or set it to `true`. Don't use `previous_response_id`; continue by sending the next response in the same conversation.

## Configure tools and skills

The Copilot harness supports:

- **Harness tools** for reading files, writing files, running shell commands, fetching web content, and delegating to subagents. New agents have all five tools enabled unless you [configure the harness tools](#configure-harness-tools).
- **Skills** referenced at the top level of the prompt agent definition.
- **Function tools** that your application executes and returns outputs for. See [Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/function-calling).
- **Foundry web search** added directly to the prompt agent definition without a project connection. The **Web** harness tool is separate and fetches content from a URL.
- **Compatible declared tools** that Foundry supplies through a managed toolbox. For the current list and each tool's configuration guidance, see [Create and manage a toolbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/toolbox#feature-support).

Tool availability can also depend on the project's region and model. A tool's existing authentication, connection, approval, and regional requirements still apply.

In `azure.yaml`, the prompt agent uses separate fields to attach capabilities and order their deployment:

| Agent field | What it does                                                                                                 |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `tools`     | Configures harness tools and directly attached declared tools.                                               |
| `skills`    | Attaches skills to the prompt agent.                                                                         |
| `toolboxes` | Attaches shared toolboxes to the prompt agent.                                                               |
| `uses`      | Orders sibling services for deployment. Adding a service to `uses` doesn't attach it to the agent by itself. |

Declare skills, connections, and toolboxes as sibling entries under `services`. Then reference their service keys from the agent's `skills`, `toolboxes`, and `uses` lists as shown in the following sections.
